nodes.name: Chemical corrosion and growth on NF
nodes.procedure: NiMo/Int/NF was synthesized by soaking NF in a molybdate peroxide solution at 80 °C for 24 h to undergo chemical corrosion on the substrate and grow a nickel molybdate precursor. SEM and XPS results indicate chemical corrosion occurred during the initial 2 h, followed by the growth of the catalytic layer.

nodes.description: HER performance in alkaline and neutral media
nodes.source_text: The HER activity of NiMo/Int/NF was evaluated in an alkaline electrolyte using Hg/HgO as the reference electrode and a graphite plate as the counter electrode... overpotential of 80.2 ± 3.53 mV and durability (stable for 5000 h) at 1000 mAcm−2 in 1 M KOH... also showed good HER performance in alkaline seawater.

The NiMo/Int/NF-catalyzed noble metal-free AEM-WE device achieves a lower cell voltage (1.78 V) at 1000 mAcm−2 and 25 °C... the cell voltage of CAPist-L1//NiMo/Int/NF is stable at ≈ 1.8 V (1000 mAcm−2) for 3000 h, with a small degradation rate of 22.8 μVh−1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cross-sectional SEM reveals a dense interlayer anchoring a rod-like, porous catalytic layer to the NF substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cross-sectional SEM images indicate a dense interlayer, which serves as a glue to tightly anchor the catalytic layer on the NF (Figure 1b; Figure S1c ...)

properties.description: Scanning Electron Microscopy image showing a layered nanostructure
properties.label: b

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder and in situ XRD identify orthorhombic NiMo alloy and monoclinic MoO2; in situ data shows a reversible decrease in MoO2 (110) crystallinity during catalysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns indicated that the NiMo/Int/NF heterostructure contains an orthorhombic NiMo alloy and monoclinic MoO2 (Figure 1c) ... in situ XRD measurements show that the full width at half maximum increases from an open circuit potential (OCP) to −0.10 V (Figure S20...)

properties.description: Plot showing the change in peak width (FWHM) during an electrochemical process.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge shows Ni-Ni/Mo scattering confirming NiMo alloy; Mo K-edge shows Mo-O shells similar to MoO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EXAFS spectrum of the Ni K-edge shows a stronger Ni-Ni/Mo scattering path ... Mo K-edge also confirms that the Mo-O shells of NiMo/Int/NF are similar to those of MoO2 (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Reveals numerous MoO2 and NiMo nanoparticles; (400) and (133) lattice planes of NiMo alloy observed via HAADF-STEM/FFT.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HR-TEM revealed numerous MoO2 and NiMo nanoparticles ... confirmed the presence of the (400) and (133) lattice planes in the NiMo alloy (Figure 1g,h).

nodes.characterization_summary: Confirms uniform distribution of Ni, Mo, and O across both the interlayer and catalytic layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDX confirmed the same elemental composition of Ni, Mo, and O for the interlayer and catalytic layer (Figure S2 ...)

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows an increase in local pH during HER, evidenced by changes in HCO3- and CO3 2- intensities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: in situ Raman measurements were conducted ... the local pH of NiMo/Int/NF increased during the HER ... (Figure 2b,c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Bode plots show low-frequency peaks (1-5 Hz) associated with the Volmer step as the rate-determining step.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) reveals peaks at 1 - 5 Hz in the Bode plot ... low-frequency signal is associated with the Volmer step.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiMo/Int/NF shows lower indentation depth (h_max = 636.9 nm) compared to NiMo/NF, indicating higher compressive strength.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nanoindentation measurements indicate a lower maximum indentation depth (hmax, 636.9 ± 37.1 nm) ... compared to NiMo/NF without an interlayer (hmax of 2163.9 ± 67.5 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: Confirms a strong adhesion force between the catalytic layer and the substrate due to the interlayer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: nanoscratch measurements confirm a strong adhesion force between the catalytic layer and the substrate for NiMo/Int/NF (Figure 3b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ XPS results verify the chemical corrosion process and the growth of the catalytic layer, with Mo and Ni species tracked over time.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on the ex situ SEM and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) results, chemical corrosion occurred during the initial 2 h ... (Figures S5 and S6, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Grazing incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD) confirms that the interlayer and catalytic layer share the same NiMo/MoO2 structure but differ in crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The grazing incidence X-ray diffraction (GIXRD) patterns revealed the same NiMo/MoO2 structure of the interlayer and catalytic layer, but their crystallinity differs (Figure S7...)

nodes.characterization_summary: LSV curves show a low overpotential of 28.1 mV at 100 mA/cm2 and 80.2 mV at 1000 mA/cm2 in 1M KOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves show a low overpotential of 28.1 ± 2.0 mV for NiMo/Int/NF at 100 mAcm−2 ... overpotentials of NiMo/Int/NF increased slightly to 80.2 ± 3.53 ... at 1000 ... mAcm−2
